'''Michael Artin''' ({{IPA|de|ˈaʁtiːn|lang}}; born 28 June 1934) is an American [[mathematician]] and a professor emeritus in the [[MIT Mathematics Department|Massachusetts Institute of Technology Mathematics Department]], known for his  contributions to [[algebraic geometry]].<ref name="profile">[http://math.mit.edu/people/profile.php?pid=9 Faculty profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130408101114/http://math.mit.edu/people/profile.php?pid=9 |date=2013-04-08 }}, MIT mathematics department, retrieved 2011-01-03</ref><ref>{{cite LCAuth |id=n81053510}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Artin was born in [[Hamburg]], Germany, and brought up in [[Indiana]]. His parents were [[Natascha Artin Brunswick|Natalia Naumovna Jasny]] (Natascha) and [[Emil Artin]], preeminent algebraist of the 20th century of [[Armenian people|Armenian]] descent. Artin's parents left Germany in 1937, because his mother's father was [[Jewish people|Jewish]].<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Artin_Michael}}</ref> His elder sister is {{visible anchor|Karin Tate|Karin Artin}}, who was married to mathematician [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]] until the late 1980s.

Artin did his undergraduate studies at [[Princeton University]], receiving an A.B. in 1955. He then moved to [[Harvard University]], where he received a Ph.D. in 1960 under the supervision of [[Oscar Zariski]], defending a thesis about [[Enriques surfaces]].<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=22863}}</ref>

In the early 1960s, Artin spent time at the [[IHÉS]] in France, contributing to the [[SGA4]] volumes of the [[Séminaire de géométrie algébrique]], on [[topos theory]] and [[étale cohomology]], jointly with [[Alexander Grothendieck]]. He also collaborated with [[Barry Mazur]] to define [[étale homotopy type|étale homotopy theory]] which has become an important tool in algebraic geometry, and applied ideas from algebraic geometry (such as the [[Nash equilibrium]]) to the study of [[diffeomorphism]]s of [[compact manifold]]s.

His work on the problem of characterising the [[representable functor]]s in the [[category of schemes]] has led to the [[Artin approximation theorem]] in [[local algebra]] as well as the "Existence theorem". This work also gave rise to the ideas of an [[algebraic space]] and [[algebraic stack]], and has proved very influential in [[moduli theory]].

He also has made important contributions to the [[deformation theory]] of algebraic varieties, serving as the basis for all future work in this area of algebraic geometry. With [[Peter Swinnerton-Dyer]], he provided a resolution of the Shafarevich-Tate conjecture for elliptic [[K3 surface]]s and the pencil of elliptic curves over finite fields.

He contributed to the theory of surface singularities which are both fundamental and seminal. The [[rational singularity]] and fundamental cycles, which are used in matroid theory, are such examples of his sheer originality and thinking.

He began to turn his interest from [[algebraic geometry]] to [[noncommutative algebra]] ([[noncommutative ring]] theory), especially geometric aspects, after a talk by [[Shimshon Amitsur]] and an encounter in [[University of Chicago]] with [[Claudio Procesi]] and Lance W. Small, "which prompted [his] first foray into ring theory".<ref>From the MacTutor biography: "His main research area changed from algebraic geometry to noncommutative ring theory".</ref> Today, he is a recognized world authority in [[noncommutative algebraic geometry]].

== Awards ==
In 2002, Artin won the [[American Mathematical Society]]'s annual [[Leroy P. Steele Prizes|Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement.

In 2005, he was awarded the [[Harvard Centennial Medal]].

In 2013, he won the [[Wolf Prize in Mathematics]], and in 2015 was awarded the [[National Medal of Science]] from President [[Barack Obama]].

He is also a member of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] and a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1969),<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|access-date=25 April 2011}}</ref> the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]],<ref name="profile" /> and the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-03.</ref>

He is a Foreign Member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and Honorary Fellow of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]], and was awarded honorary doctorates from the universities of Hamburg and [[Antwerp]], [[Belgium]]. He was invited to give a talk on the topic "The Étale Topology of Schemes" at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1966 in [[Moscow]], [[USSR]].

==Books==
===As author===
*with Barry Mazur: {{cite book|title=Etale homotopy|location=Berlin; Heidelberg; New York|publisher=Springer|year=1969}}
*{{cite book|title=Algebraic spaces|location=New Haven|publisher=Yale University Press|year=1971}}
*{{cite book|title=Théorie des topos et cohomologie étale des schémas|location=Berlin; New York|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=1972}}
*in collaboration with Alexandru Lascu & Jean-François Boutot: {{cite book|title=Théorèmes de représentabilité pour les espaces algébriques|location=Montréal|publisher=Presses de l'Université de Montréal|year=1973}}
*with notes by C.S. Sephardi & Allen Tannenbaum: {{cite book|title=Lectures on deformations of singularities|location=Bombay|publisher=Tata Institute of Fundamental Research|year=1976}}
*{{cite book|title=Algebra|location=Englewood Cliffs, N.J.|publisher=Prentice Hall|year=1991}} {{cite book|title=2nd edition|location=Boston|publisher=Pearson Education|year=2011}}<ref>{{cite web|author=Karaali, Gizem|title=Review of ''Algebra'' by Michael Artin|date=24 March 2011|website=MAA Reviews, Mathematical Association of America|url=https://old.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/algebra-0}}</ref>
*{{cite book |title=Algebraic Geometry: Notes on a Course |date=2022 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |url=https://bookstore.ams.org/view?ProductCode=GSM/222}}

===As editor===
*with David Mumford: {{cite book|title=Contributions to algebraic geometry in honor of Oscar Zariski|location=Baltimore|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press|year=1979}}
*with John Tate: {{cite book|title=Arithmetic and geometry : papers dedicated to I.R. Shafarevich on the occasion of his sixtieth birthday|location=Boston|publisher=Birkhäuser|year=1983}}
*with Hanspeter Kraft & [[Reinhold Remmert]]: {{cite book|title=Duration and change : fifty years at Oberwolfach|location=Berlin; New York|publisher=Springer-Verlag|year=1994}}
